newsitem.title: CANADA: Alcan to report development on Kemano talks.
newsitem.headline: Alcan to report development on Kemano talks.

text.p: Alcan Aluminium Ltd and the province of British Columbia said on Monday they plan to make an "important announcement" on Tuesday regarding talks on resolving issues surrounding the company's Kemano Completion Project.

Alcan officials declined to elaborate, but a spokesman for B.C. Premier Glen Clark said the announcement was "good news," and it would be made jointly by the premier and Alcan chief executive officer Jacques Bougie at a press conference in Vancouver.

Alcan and the B.C. government had been in talks on resolving the issue, in which the company was seeking compensation for its Kemano hydroelectric project, which the government ordered cancelled in 1995 after it was half-completed.
Alcan wrote down its US$420 million investment in the cancelled project in the third quarter of 1995, and sued the provincial government for compensation.
Discussions between the two have focussed on the province selling power to Alcan at the same cost the Kemano plant would have provided.
The province introduced legislation last Wednesday paving way for such an agreement. Alcan welcomed the legislation, saying it moved the two sides closer to an agreement.
The additional hydroelectric power would be needed if Alcan decided to go ahead with a possible C$1 billion expansion of its aluminum smelter in Kitimat, B.C.
